about.title: About
paragraphs: I am a senior frontend engineer and interface designer who loves building digital stuff that makes sense. My background is rooted in the startup ecosystem, where being resourceful and agile isn't an option—it's the core of the job.

I'm a generalist at heart who decided to specialize in the frontend. Because of that, I don't just “paint screens”; I understand the APIs, the architecture, and the technical trade-offs behind every user interaction.

When I'm not tweaking Tailwind tokens or refining layouts, I'm usually thinking about product strategy or disconnected, working with my hands on physical engineering and high-end woodworking projects.

rely.thesis: A Hub of Stations: live Preview with an OK/KO on the piece, and a Recipe graph engineers deploy to the floor.
rely.result: In production on factory floors, multi-tenant / multi-site. Hub in the cloud, an agent per Station on the line.
rely.previewAlt: Station Preview with a live PCB camera feed, piece identity, defect count, and OK/KO totals
rely.previewCaption: Preview is the floor: the piece, a verdict, OK/KO/Rework. The red card is the status, not a chart.

decisions.title: The Station is the product
decisions.content: The Hub is a list of Stations, not a model zoo. Opening one is the floor: live camera, piece identity, OK/KO. The operator reads a verdict. Recipes, overlays, and analytics sit beside that surface — they do not replace it.

decisions.title: A Recipe is a graph you deploy
decisions.content: Inspection is not a script per line. Trigger → images → detect → Evaluación is a visual flow with a contextual inspector. Evaluación is a rule on detections (count, confidence) that writes a station status: OK if it holds, KO if it does not. Deploy publishes the Recipe; the canvas draft is not what the floor is running.

decisions.title: Overlays are the operator language
decisions.content: Detections have to be readable on the image: label corner, dashed ROI, human vs model. That overlay is configured per Station so Preview and review share the same picture language — status is the color, not the class name.

loadzone.thesis: One club, two products — an operational staff scan of wellness and load, and a player check-in that is one question at a time. The Streak Cromo is the identity that grows with that habit.
loadzone.cromoCaption: Streak Cromo in the player phone. Tilt it. Material names stay off the card; the foil is the reward.

decisions.title: Wellness and load at a glance
decisions.content: Coordinators need the squad in one operational scan before and after the Session: recovery, energy, soreness, sleep hours, sleep quality, then POST RPE. Missing DailyEntry stays a dash — the table does not invent completeness. Color is a triage signal, not a FIFA dump. This surface is not the Streak Cromo.

decisions.title: One question at a time
decisions.content: Check-in is not a clipboard. PRE and POST are separate moments on the Session, but each form is one WellnessMetric at a time: large type, a thumb-sized slider, labels at the ends, a count of what is still missing. Identity (the Cromo) sits after the fill, not as a second questionnaire.

decisions.title: Exercises that actually build Sessions
decisions.content: Staff do not author a Session from a blank page. An Exercise is a drill with duration, pitch size, player count, then a short tactical classification. Creating one is a form with defaults and dropdowns. Placing Exercises on a Session is how the week becomes real.
